newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks shrug off President Kim's speech.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks shrug off President Kim's speech.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's apology on Friday over election campaign spending abuses did not affect the Seoul stock market, which staged a consolidation after hitting a new yearly high, brokers said.
Kim, seeking to defuse a political crisis and rescue his administration, apologised on live television over election campaign spending abuses.
But he again insisted it would be impossible to reveal details of his own spending in the 1992 presidential elections.
"His speech has nothing substantial. The market had not expected anything," said Cha Hee-gun of Sunkyong Securities.

"He revealed no details linked with election funds as expected," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities. "The market is not affected by external factors and is focusing more on an economic recovery and falling interest rates."
The composite stock index shed 0.70 of a point to 741.80 at 0130 GMT on a consolidation in reaction to recent steep rises.
Brokers said they expected the market to rebound if the index deepened its correction. They said the underlying market sentiment still remained solid.
